article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Evening Brief
article.dek: Lamar Jackson is officially out, the Eagles fly to London without Barkley, and the board re-dealt one card before Sunday.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson officially out — Huntley starts Sunday night
paragraphs: The watch is over. Baltimore ruled out Lamar Jackson (ankle) on Friday, and head coach Jesse Minter named Tyler Huntley the starter for Sunday night at Atlanta. Jackson missed all three practices this week.

It doesn't stop at quarterback. New starting center Cam Jurgens (concussion) and edge rusher Trey Hendrickson (finger) are also out. Questionable: cornerback Marlon Humphrey, receiver Zay Flowers and guard Andrew Vorhees. On the Falcons' side, linebacker Yasir Abdullah is out and four players are questionable, including left tackle Jake Matthews.

The app already prices the contingency: Huntley is listed as Baltimore's expected starter. The line told the story through the day — DraftKings moved Atlanta from -3.0 to -3.5, joining the rest of the board. Sunday night kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET.
items.takeaway: Sunday night's price already knows Huntley is the quarterback. Your edge is the exact number your book hangs — run it through Check.

items.headline: Eagles fly to London without Barkley
paragraphs: Philadelphia officially ruled out Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Sunday's London game against Jacksonville — along with DeVonta Smith, Marquise Brown, Drew Kendall and Marcus Epps. Barkley didn't practice all week. Will Shipley is projected to start with Tank Bigsby on injured reserve.

Two more moving parts: Jalen Hurts popped up on the injury report Friday with a calf but was a full participant with no designation, and the offensive line is being rebuilt on the fly after Lane Johnson's retirement and the Cam Jurgens trade to Baltimore.
London kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET — first game of the day, and the one where news travels slowest. Confirm the final backfield picture in the morning board before it, not after.
items.takeaway: First kickoff of Sunday gets the first check. Don't lock anything for London until the morning board is in.

items.headline: Sunday weather: Washington and Pittsburgh stay wet
paragraphs: Final kickoff-window reads for the 1:00 p.m. ET outdoor games. MetLife (Browns at Jets) dried out since morning: 69F, light wind with gusts to 15. The wet ones held: Northwest Stadium (Giants at Commanders) 70F with rain, and Acrisure (Colts at Steelers) 66F with rain. Both have only light wind, around 7 mph.
London (Eagles at Jaguars, 9:30 a.m. ET): 58F, mostly cloudy, no rain. The late games and domes look fine.
Weather is a condition, not an edge. It tells you what kind of game to expect — not who wins it.
items.takeaway: Pack for rain in Washington and Pittsburgh; everywhere else looks playable.

items.headline: Quarterback room: no new changes
paragraphs: The evening QB feed matches the morning: Huntley for Baltimore (now confirmed by the team), Cam Ward still Tennessee's starter, Jameis Winston still the Giants' starter, Tyson Bagent still Chicago's. Nothing else moved.
If a starter changes after this board, inactives are the signal — about 90 minutes before kickoff.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate stays Minnesota — the likeliest winner, not the best price
paragraphs: The Hit Rate card is Minnesota moneyline -134 at FanDuel. The app gives the Vikings a 0.694 model probability, trust 0.629, reliability LOW. The moneyline drifted from -136 to -134 through the day; the spread never moved off -2.5.

Hit Rate means one thing: which supported pick looks most likely to win. It forgoes value for win probability — the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. A higher win chance at a shorter price is the whole idea, not a flaw. The evaluator prices a -135 play-through.

items.headline: Balanced re-dealt: Chicago moneyline -122
paragraphs: Balanced moved off Indianapolis +2.5 and onto Bears moneyline -122 at DraftKings. Model probability 0.570, trust 0.550, 0.75 units, reliability LOW, evaluator play-through -123.

The timing isn't a coincidence: Pittsburgh moved from -2.5 to -3.0 at DraftKings and Pinnacle during the day, which shortened the Colts' number. When the board changes, the lane re-deals. Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much — and it found a new one.

items.headline: Value holds: 49ers +3.0
paragraphs: Value is back a second straight board: San Francisco +3.0 at -104 on FanDuel against Seattle. Model probability 0.505, barely +EV, MEDIUM reliability. Value is always the model's +EV play — it shows up when the bar is cleared and goes quiet when it isn't.

The hook note from this morning still matters: Pinnacle has Seattle at -3.5 while FanDuel sits at -3.0. Same game, different hook. If your book hangs -3.5 instead of -3.0, the value isn't the same — tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet/no-bet verdict on YOUR price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

items.headline: The hook — the half point that matters most
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine a team favored by 3.0 wins by exactly 3 points. If you bet them at -3.0, that's a push — your money comes back. If you bet them at -3.5, that same 3-point win is a loss.

One half point decided everything. That's the hook: the half point past a key number. Key numbers are the most common margins of victory — 3 and 7, because of how football scoring works — so a hook around them is worth more than a hook anywhere else.
items.takeaway: A line of -3.0 and a line of -3.5 are not the same bet. Always price the exact number your book offers, not the one you wish it offered.

items.headline: Baltimore-Atlanta: DraftKings joins -3.5
paragraphs: This morning's split is gone. DraftKings hung Atlanta -3.0 while FanDuel and Pinnacle sat at -3.5; this evening DraftKings moved to -3.5, joining the rest of the board. Friday's official Lamar Jackson ruling was the trigger.
One number everywhere now. If your book still shows -3.0, that's your price to check — not the board's.

items.headline: Pittsburgh -2.5 becomes -3.0; Balanced walks away from the Colts
paragraphs: The Steelers moved from -2.5 to -3.0 at DraftKings and Pinnacle during the day. FanDuel still shows -2.5 — shop it if that's your book.

The app's Balanced card moved with it: off Colts +2.5, onto Bears moneyline. The market and the card told the same story. A move through the 3 matters more than most moves, because 3 is the most common margin in football.

items.headline: Minnesota moneyline drifts to -134; cards re-dealt
paragraphs: The Vikings' moneyline ticked from -136 to -134 at FanDuel; DraftKings sits at -142. Spreads held at -2.5. Small drift on the favorite's price, steady spreads — the morning board had most of it, the evening board confirms it.

The evening re-deal: Hit Rate (Minnesota moneyline) and Value (49ers +3.0) held their lanes; Balanced changed (Colts +2.5 to Bears moneyline -122). If your book's number isn't the board's, tap Check and type in your line and price — the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a verdict on YOUR price.

items.headline: Sunday inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff — that's your last filter
paragraphs: This evening board is the last full refresh before Sunday. The one thing it can't carry: Sunday's inactive lists, which post about 90 minutes before each kickoff. That's where a questionable tag becomes a real absence.

Make Sunday morning a two-step: read the morning brief, then run anything that moved through Check with your book's live price. And the honesty nudge — settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Inactives, then Check, then kickoff. In that order.
